chapter: Dance halls and clubs of the 1930s
title: The original 25 Club and the Honeysuckle Inn
summary: Two rival roadhouses in Prohibition days, where everything cost 25 cents.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yeah, that's right. We had a good little band at the original 25 Club. That was back off the Pontchartrain Road where the Honeysuckle Inn was. You may have heard of the Honeysuckle Inn. The Honeysuckle Inn and the original 25 Club were right across from each other. Is that? Sharky opened at the original 25 Club and then left there and went across the street to the Honeysuckle Inn. And I was playing over at the original 25 Club with Eddie Miller and Bill Padron. And I think Sharky was playing over at the other, at the Honeysuckle Inn at that time. It was a real keen rivalry between two places. The boss of the Honeysuckle Inn used to stand out with a lantern because it had no electric light, there was no street lights and they had to use an old lantern. And they had the 25 Club hired a man and they'd both be standing out there with lanterns flagging the cars down as they'd come down the road, you know. So one didn't turn out to a free fall.
There's a place, I think one day I was at the market with Bob Coquille, do you remember that? It was about the original 2 Bits Club, is that the same thing?

The original 2 Bits Club, that's it. That's right. That's what, everything was 25 cents. Did they sell whiskey? No, that was in prohibition days. They couldn't sell whiskey. That's why they charged 25 cents. A bowl of ice was 25, a Coca-Cola was 25. The sandwich was 25 cents. Anything you ordered was 25 cents. And of course if you brought your own bottle of whiskey in, you paid 25 cents for the privilege of bringing in your own whiskey. And they did pretty good business too, even at that. I also played at the Honey Circle Inn, even before these days. I played out there, I believe it was about 26 or 27, with a little band with Steve Massico, and Steve Massico played outdoor sax. Very good. A fellow by the name of Henry Ferriero played banjo, and a fellow by the name of Fitch Flick played drums. And I waited out there for quite a while. That's what I'll take.
